fields.answer: (i) Presbyopia — the eye lens loses flexibility and ciliary muscles weaken with age, so the near point recedes. (ii) Convex lens reading glasses, or bifocal/progressive lenses. (iii) A pilot must read near instruments and see far outside, so both ranges must be clear. (iv) P = +2 D. (v) Yes — bifocal/progressive lenses (upper part for distance, lower convex +2 D part for near) give clear vision at all distances.
fields.finalAnswer: Presbyopia; corrected by convex (bifocal/progressive) lenses; required power = +2 D (convex lens of focal length 50 cm).
solutionSteps: [1 mark] (i) The defect is presbyopia. With age the eye lens loses its flexibility and the ciliary muscles weaken, so the eye cannot accommodate for near objects; the near point recedes while distant vision stays normal.
[1 mark] (ii) A convex lens of suitable power (reading glasses), or bifocal/progressive lenses: upper part for distant vision, lower convex part for near vision.

[1 mark] (iii) As a pilot he must read nearby cockpit instruments and also watch distant objects outside; uncorrected presbyopia could make instrument reading unreliable, so his correction must give clear near and far vision.
[1 mark] (iv) Object at u = −25 cm must form a virtual image at the near point v = −50 cm. 1/f = 1/v − 1/u = −1/50 + 1/25 = +1/50 cm⁻¹, so f = +50 cm = +0.5 m and P = 1/f = +2 D (convex lens).

[1 mark] (v) Since his distant vision is normal, no correction (or very weak) is needed in the upper part; bifocal or progressive lenses with +2 D in the lower part let him see clearly at all distances, which suits his profession.

solutionSteps: [1 mark] (1) Ingestion: Amoeba (unicellular, holozoic heterotroph) puts out pseudopodia (finger-like projections) that surround and engulf the food particle, forming a food vacuole.
[1 mark] (2) Digestion: digestive enzymes from the cytoplasm enter the food vacuole and break complex food into simple, soluble molecules.
[1 mark] (3) Absorption: the simple digested molecules diffuse out of the food vacuole into the cytoplasm.
[1 mark] (4) Assimilation: the absorbed nutrients are used by the cell to obtain energy and for growth and repair.
[1 mark] (5) Egestion: the undigested residue is moved to the cell surface and thrown out when the vacuole ruptures there.

fields.questionText: We need to water the soil in plants on a regular basis. But it ultimately reaches the leaves of the plant. Explain how this takes place.
fields.answer: Water absorbed by the roots moves up through the continuous xylem vessels of root, stem and leaves. Loss of water vapour through stomata of leaves (transpiration) creates a suction force, the transpiration pull, which pulls the water column up from the roots to the leaves.
fields.finalAnswer: Water rises through xylem from roots to leaves, pulled up by the transpiration pull created by loss of water vapour through the stomata.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Roots absorb water from the soil; it moves up through the interconnected xylem vessels of root, stem and leaves.
[1 mark] Evaporation of water through stomata of leaves (transpiration) creates a suction force (transpiration pull) that pulls the water column up to the leaves.

rationale: Merged OR alternatives split: kept alternative (a) (water transport via transpiration pull) as a clean 2-mark question; stray '2 OR (b)...' removed; answer/steps rewritten to sum to 2.

fields.questionText:
Pravin was given a list of characteristics associated with the process of anaerobic respiration in humans:
(i) Location — Muscle cell
(ii) Condition — Requires presence of oxygen (O2) and carbon dioxide (CO2)
(iii) End product — 3-carbon molecules
Which of the above characteristics is/are related to this process?
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Correct option: (b) (i) and (iii). Anaerobic respiration occurs in muscle cells during lack of oxygen and converts pyruvate into lactic acid, a 3-carbon molecule; it does not require oxygen, so (ii) is wrong.
